News.title: Meghan Markle takes a leaf out of Princess Kate’s book on sailing trip in Sydney on ‘pseudo-royal’ tour
News.content:
MEGHAN Markle has the wind in her sails – as she takes a leaf out of Princess Kate’s style book during a boat trip Down Under.

Meg, 44, stunned in blue and white stripes during the Sussexes “pseudo-royal” tour in Australia – coincidentally mirroring Kate’s sailing attire.





The Duchess of Sussex was pictured laughing and smiling in her shirt as she joined members of Invictus Australia in Sydney Harbour.

And it seems the colour combination is a popular look – with the Princess of Wales also opting for blue and white while on a similar visit in 2014.

Kate, 44, sported the stripy look while on America’s Cup yacht in Auckland Harbour during a three-week tour of Australia and New Zealand.



Meg was snapped aboard the vessel with Prince Harry – as the pair marked the end of their own four-day faux royal tour.

The boat was filled with former participants of Invictus Games – Harry’s sporting event for wounded personnel and veterans.

They chatted with veterans and their families, before being gifted flip-flops – jokingly labelled with “G-Day Hazza” and “G’day Megs” on them.

Before boarding the boat, Harry shared a sweet moment with four-year-old Charlotte – the daughter of veteran Joel Vanderzwan.



The Duke of Sussex, 41, danced with the youngster before heading out onto the water with his wife.

While the fashion may have been similar, Kate and Will’s boating trip had a much more competitive edge.

The then-Duke and Duchess of Cambridge battled against each other during “informal” yacht races.

Kate proved she ruled the waves after taking to the wheel of the 80ft vessel and trouncing her husband in two races.

Meghan had previously shrugged off her royal title and told Aussies to simply “call me Meg” while meeting crowds.



Insiders told The Sun the four-day trip to Oz has acted as a dummy run and testing ground for a potential joint tour of the UK.

At one point, Meg made a surprise TV appearance on MasterChef Australia – starring as an expert judge on the cooking show.



And she told university students to be “strong” in the face of social media bullying as she discussed the impacts have on young people.

The Duchess opened up on her own social media experiences, telling them she was “the most trolled person in the world”.

Meg said: “I can speak to that really personally, which is why I like to listen, because it rings true for me in a very real way.

“For now, 10 years, every day for 10 years, I have been bullied and attacked. And I was the most trolled person in the entire world.

“I’m still here.”



Harry also opened up on his mental health struggles – revealing how he had to “cleanse” himself of the past before having kids.

The Duke attended a summit focusing on mental health, with tickets for attendance in Melbourne selling at an eye-watering Aus$997 (£706).

Speaking at the Whitten Oval, home of AFL club the Western Bulldogs, he compared his parenting skills to those of his mother and father.

The Duke was quick to insist that he was not “pointing the finger” at his own parents.

He went on to say that even someone with a perfect upbringing would want to improve on it for their own children.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Harry said: “I see parenting evolving over time. Our kids are our upgrade.

“Not to say that I upgraded my dad or that my kids upgraded me, but the kids that we bring up in today’s world need to be upgraded.”

News.title: It will take two YEARS for world to recover from shortages sparked by Iran war, energy chief warns as fuel crisis looms
News.content:
A HUGE fuel crisis is looming as the head of the International Energy Agency has warned it will take two years for supplies to recover from the war in Iran.

Fatih Birol said oil and gas supplies would take “approximately two years overall to reach pre-war levels again” after warning yesterday that Europe has just six weeks of jet fuel left.





Energy prices have soared since the start of March after Iran closed off the Strait in response to US-Israeli blitzes of the rogue nation.

Iranians refused to re-open the Strait last week, even though free flow through the shipping lane was a key plank in a two-week ceasefire agreement.

Now the US navy is enforcing a blockade of the shipping lane that applies to any ships visiting Iranian ports.



But even if the conflict ends with upcoming peace talks, energy supplies may take two years to recover, experts have warned.

Energy chief Birol added that this “will vary from country to country – in Iraq, for example, it will take much longer than in Saudi Arabia”.

He warned that markets are not taking seriously enough the effects of a the Strait of Hormuz being shut for a long time.

Although many shipments were already out of the Middle East and on their way across the world when the war broke out, those tankers have now arrived at their destinations.



Birol explained: “But no new tankers were loaded in March. There were no new deliveries of oil, gas or fuels to Asian markets.

“This gap is now becoming apparent. If the Strait of Hormuz is not reopened, we must prepare for significantly higher energy prices.”

He added that the IEA was ready to act immediately and decisively after it released a huge 400 million barrels of oil from its reserves last month.

It comes as Birol warned yesterday that Europe has just six weeks of jet fuel left, as vital supplies remain blocked by the war in Iran.

Mass flight cancellations will begin “soon” if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, he said.



Birol’s deadline means airports could face critical fuel shortages by May, causing travel chaos for Brits heading abroad during the school May half-term holidays.

A number of airports in Italy have already warned that they were running out of fuel.



And British Airways has announced it will permanently axe its service from London Heathrow to Jeddah in Saudi Arabia from April 24.

A number of airlines have had to reduce their flight schedule to avoid spiralling costs.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

United Airlines is the latest to confirm that it would be cutting five per cent of flights – around 250 a month – in the second and third quarters of 2026.

It comes as a former government advisor warned Brits should be preparing for World War Two-style food rationing with shortages of supermarket staples such as beer and meat as well as common prescription drugs expected.

News.title: Nurse caught having sex in hospital THREE times on duty with colleagues hearing ‘noises that went on for 5 minutes’
News.content:
WARD ROMP Nurse caught having sex in hospital THREE times on duty with colleagues hearing ‘noises that went on for 5 minutes’

A NURSE who was caught having sex while on duty three separate times has been struck off after a colleague overheard one of the romps.

Mental health nurse Kate Sullivan was working at Glanrhyd Hospital in Bridgend, Wales, when the “unprofessional behaviour” unfolded.



A fitness to practice hearing heard that between October 2020 and Summer 2021 she had been involved in a relationship with a co-worker that she did not disclose to her employer.



Sullivan, who had been temporarily reported to a band seven ward manager, confessed that she had been in a casual relationship with a colleague.

She said: “I engaged in a casual relationship with a fellow colleague and he was working as a band two on the ward at that time.”

Sullivan worked on a secure rehabilitation unit exclusively for men which had a high intake from prison.

It was determined that she had sex with her co-worker lover on hospital grounds on three separate occasions on March 4, 2021, and January 8 and 17, 2022.



During the first of the romps, Sullivan and her lover were overheard by another colleague.

Sullivan had been on a night shift when she led a female co-worker to the hospital’s “hub shop” before making it clear to her that she wanted to be left alone with the co-worker she was in a relationship with.

The female co-worker left and went to an adjoining room where she was left feeling “very uncomfortable” after hearing sounds “consistent with sexual intercourse” coming from the room Sullivan was in.

In a witness statement the female co-worker said: “I could hear the desk was banging against the wall and I could hear them both making noises.



“There was no-one else around, and all of the patients were asleep, so I was certain the noise I heard came from them next door.

“The sex did not last very long. The noises went on for about two to five minutes.”

After the second romp, Sullivan texted the same female co-worker to say she had engaged in sexual activity in the “recharge room.”

And, after the final romp, Sullivan again texted the same female co-worker to inform her she had just had sex with a colleague in the hospital again.

The message read: “Haha [Colleague A] just had sex with me.”



Sullivan would deny the sexual activity, saying she made things up to keep her co-worker interested in talking with her.

However, the panel found it was “inherently unlikely that Miss Sullivan would have invented a story that she and Colleague A had sex in the workplace.”

Various other concerns were raised around Sullivan’s conduct, including refusing to examine a patient who had a rash on their groin.

Sullivan was also accused of breaching confidentiality by disclosing colleagues’ sickness absence reasons to other staff, the panel heard.

The now struck off mental health nurse would allegedly manipulate her rota to work alongside her lover more frequently.



She also showed up for a shift that she wasn’t scheduled to work with the panel concluding it was because her lover was on duty that day.

On one occasion Sullivan and her lover left the ward abruptly – leaving the rest of the team understaffed.

According to the panel, she would criticise other colleagues paperwork and branded one a “lazy c***.”

Another instance saw Sullivan breach professional boundaries by letting a patient into her office with the door shut and blinds down for 20 minutes.

This was particularly inappropriate given the patient’s “sexualised behaviour and difficulties in understanding boundaries.”



On two other occasions Sullivan laughed when a patient called her “babe”, hugged a patient and failed to report the same patient after he grabbed another female member of staff and grinded against her.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Sullivan was sacked for gross misconduct, bringing a seven-year career at the health board.

She did not attend the Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) fitness to practise hearing.

News.title: UK & France to hold crunch talks on Strait of Hormuz today as Trump warns Hezbollah ‘act nicely’ amid fragile ceasefire
News.content:
THE UK and France are set to hold crunch talks over the Strait of Hormuz later today to help restore the flow of trade and lower soaring global costs.

Europe is springing into action to help reopen the vital waterway after Israel and Hezbollah agreed to a 10-day ceasefire – marking a total pause in fighting in the Middle East.





Donald Trump helped broker peace in Lebanon but warned terror group Hezbollah to “act nicely” during the truce after the Iranian proxy group waged war on Israel after it bombed Tehran.

Trump hailed a “historic day for Lebanon” and vowed that the move can now allow “good things” to happen across the volatile region.

UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer is due to chair a virtual meeting at midday aimed at getting the Strait of Hormuz open.

He will tell world leaders, alongside French President Emmanuel Macron, that there is a “global responsibility” to get the major trade route back on track.

The crucial shipping lane sees a fifth of the world’s oil flow through each year but has been closed by Iran for the past six weeks due to the war.

Iran laid mines across the seabed in response to deadly strikes from the US and Israel which obliterated their chain of command.

Their plan to choke the world of oil and drive up costs has sparked economic chaos across dozens of nations.



But in recent days Trump launched his own blockade of the strait aimed to clearing the mines and regaining control from the Iranian regime.

Starmer and other allies refused to take part in Trump’s blockade. over the weekend.

French Defence Minister Catherine Vautrin has now said European countries, such as Belgium, the Netherlands and France could help to clear the explosives and secure passage through the Strait of Hormuz.

Starmer is expected to repeat these remarks during the call.

Number 10 says Starmer will say: “The unconditional and immediate reopening of the strait is a global responsibility, and we need to act to get global energy and trade flowing freely again.



“We must reassure commercial shipping and support mine clearance operations to ensure a return to global stability and security.”

Around 40 countries and the International Maritime Organisation are expected to be on today’s call which will also aim at helping to secure a permanent ceasefire.

The conference will be followed up by a multinational military planning summit at Permanent Joint Headquarters in Northwood, north-west London, next week.

This will see countries discuss a joint defensive mission in the Middle East now that the conflict is halted, Downing Street has said.



It is hoped that Trump’s blockade of the strait will allow allies to join US warships in the region without the threat of Iran attacking.

It comes as Iran’s economy continues to be in freefall with the toll of the war leaving Tehran in desperate need of a swift conclusion.

The US and Israel have caused an estimated £200billion in damage through their relentless air campaign, according to Iranian media.

The figure is the equivalent of 26 years of punishing global sanctions.



Their woes are set to worsen the longer the US controls the strait as the shipping lane provides Tehran with the majority of its annual revenue in oil.

Trump vowed on Thursday that a complete deal with Iran to end the war entirely is almost finalised.

The US president said Tehran has agreed to abandon its pursuit of a nuclear weapon for the next 20 years.

Speaking from the White House lawn, a buoyant Donald Trump proclaimed the US had finally achieved one of its major goals.

“Iran has agreed not to have a nuclear weapon; they have agreed to it very powerfully,” Trump said.



“They have agreed to give us back the nuclear dust.

“We have a lot of agreement with Iran, and I think something is going to happen very positive.”

When asked about the US blockade of Iranian ports, the president said the US is “doing very well”.

“The navy is incredible. No ship is even thinking about entering,” Trump said.

“No ship is going past our navy.”



The president also claimed Iran is unable to do “any business” while the blockade is in place.

“The blockage is maybe more powerful than the bombing, if you want to know the truth,” Trump said.

This comes after the head of the International Energy Agency warned Europe has just six weeks of jet fuel left.

IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol said mass cancellations will start “soon” if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed.

News.title: Teacher ‘flashes topless photos to stunned students in PowerPoint presentation’ as school probes ‘inappropriate images’
News.content:
SCHOOL SHAME Teacher ‘flashes topless photos to stunned students in PowerPoint presentation’ as school probes ‘inappropriate images’

A WASHINGTON teacher accidentally flashed students with topless photos during a PowerPoint presentation as the school launches probe.

The unnamed school teacher showed four nude images featuring bare breasts at Glacier Peak High School in Snohomish city in Washington.





The scandalous pics appeared in the bottom left hand corner of the teacher’s slide in a slip up which has outraged the school community.

It is not yet known whether the exposed bosom was that of the teacher or of another individual.

Headteacher Alicia Mitchell emailed parents about the shocking photos and apologised for the accident.

“We want to make you aware of an incident in a classroom where inappropriate images were inadvertently shared with the students,” Mitchell said in the letter obtained by The Post.



“It is our understanding that these images have since been viewed by many others beyond the classroom and [we] want to give you an opportunity to process with your student if you choose to do so. The content included images of nude breasts and were briefly visible during a teacher’s PowerPoint presentation.”

She added that the nude photos did not reflect the school’s “expectations for classroom materials.”

The teacher has not yet been named, and it is not clear why they had photos of breasts on their computer nor whether they have been suspended.

Seattle Red radio host and columnist Jason Rantz has seen a screenshot of the offending PowerPoint presentation and said that the boob pics looked like “previews of photos from a folder”.



The school has launched an internal investigation into the disturbing blunder.

A spokesperson from Glacier Peak High School said: “We take this matter seriously and are following established processes to review the situation and determine next steps.”

They declined to comment further, saying: “As this is a personnel matter currently under investigation, we’re unable to provide additional details or comment further”.

It follows the sentencing of one sick pigtailed social worker who groomed and sexually assaulted a prepubescent boy.

Chloe Rose Castro faces 20 years behind bars after having a sexual relationship with a sixth-grade boy.



The exact age of the boy is not known, but pupils in the sixth grade are between 11 and 12 years old.

The married social worker asked the boy to be her boyfriend, according to court documents, and the pair planned to move to New Mexico.

News.title: Illegal migrants who lie to get visas will have benefits axed after rogue lawyers tell asylum seekers to pose as GAY
News.content:
ILLEGAL migrants who lie to get visas will have their benefits axed – after it emerged lawyers are telling asylum seekers to pretend to be gay.

The Home Secretary wants new powers to strip asylum seekers of support if they break the law or don’t follow Home Office rules.





Shabana Mahmood is seeking approval for the new powers to bar migrants from getting state support.

If approved, this would move away from the requirement to support “destitute” asylum seekers, brought in under EU law in 2005.

It would allow Ms Mahmood to deny support to migrants who have the right to work after a year of waiting for asylum and can support themselves.

Anyone who refuses to leave the country or enters illegally won’t be entitled to financial support, according to The Telegraph.

This would also go for migrants who break the law or refuse to relocate to cheaper accommodation.

This comes after the Home Office launched an investigation into claims that dodgy legal advisers are telling migrants to lie in order to get a visa.

A Government spokesman said it would hold any lawyers, advisers or migrants involved to account.



“Both the Home Office and Immigration Advice Authority are investigating the claims made by the BBC, both yesterday and today, to ensure anyone potentially abusing our immigration system is held accountable.

“Any attempt to misuse protections designed to protect genuine victims from the devastation of domestic abuse is shameful and completely unacceptable.

“The Home Secretary has been clear that those trying to defraud the British people to remain in the UK will have their application refused and find themselves on a one way flight out of Britain.

“Where unethical and illegal practices are identified and evidence exists, legal practitioners will be referred to the police through the relevant regulatory body.”



The BBC sent a reporter undercover to expose shady legal advisers who are telling migrants to pretend to be gay or abused.

Both men and women are reportedly marrying, moving to the UK and then making fake domestic abuse claims to get fast-track residency.

Migrants can apply for permission to settle in the UK permanently if their relationship has broken down because of domestic violence or abuse.

But an increasing number are fabricating allegations to exploit this, with more than 5,500 a year claiming residency under this scheme.



The BBC found an immigration adviser online who – unprompted – suggested making a fake abuse claim and charged £900 to make up a story to the Home Office.

The adviser said “don’t worry, I’ll create one (a story)” to feed to the Home Office.

He then goes on to feed the undercover reporter a story about how the fake abuse unfolded, stemming from an argument.

Problems with this immigration route were highlighted a decade ago.

A report by the Independent Chief Inspector of Borders and Immigration identified issues with checks being made of domestic abuse claims and “unverified evidence”.



Another shock investigation also revealed lawyers are helping migrants and their wives pose as gay so they can stay in the UK.

Rogue advisers provide fabricated cover stories and testimony from fake partners, while charging thousands of pounds in the asylum scam.

These fake claims are being used by migrants, often whose student or work visas have expired.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In an attempt to avoid being booted out of the country, they claim to be in fear for their lives if they return to their home country.

One reporter was even told that once he won his false case, he could bring his wife over from Pakistan and she could also claim to be a lesbian.

News.title: Ex-Dem lawmaker Justin Fairfax acted ‘very strange’ months before shock murder-suicide as pal reveals ‘final straw’
News.content:
A LONGTIME friend of ex-democratic lawmaker Justin Fairfax has revealed his unusual behavior months before he killed his wife and himself in a horrifying murder-suicide.

The 47-year-old shot and killed his wife Cerina, 49, in the basement of their $1million home before going to the bedroom and killing himself while their two teenage children were at home, cops said on Thursday.





Fairfax County Police Chief Kevin Davis said the former Virginia Lieutenant Governor carried out the shocking homicide amid an ongoing “domestic dispute surrounding what seems to be a complicated or messy divorce.”

After being together for two decades, the couple separated in 2024 but were still living in the same Annandale home as their divorce proceedings continued.

Chilling audio footage revealed that the Democrat’s teenage son was forced to call 911 after finding his mom bleeding on the ground with several gunshot wounds, that he initially thought were stab wounds.

Now, Dr. Patricia King, city councilmember in Chesapeake City and longtime friend of Fairfax, has spoken out about his “very strange” behavior leading up to the horrifying incident.



King had been friends with Fairfax for over a decade and helped him launch his political career.

Speaking to The U.S. Sun, she confirmed the couple had been struggling privately in recent years.

“There have been a lot of things that have happened over the last few

years, a lot of very tragic things, and Justin had his personal struggles,” Dr King said.

“He was a very kind, thoughtful, generous person and he must have been in a very, very bad place for this to have happened.”



Signs that something was not right with the former lieutenant governor began months before the murder-suicide, King revealed upon reflection.

She noted his unusual behavior after they last spoke a few months ago.

“I kind of lost contact with him over the last few months which I thought was very strange because there was a time when we talking like three or four times a week for hours about everything,” she said.

“So I did notice that there was a little bit of distance, but I just assumed he was busy with his practice and family and son’s sports.



“You know, sometimes people just get busy and they’re not in as close of contact. So that’s kind of what I assumed. I just could not have imagined this.”

In divorce court filings seen by The U.S. Sun, Cerina claimed that her husband was suffering with alcohol issues and isolating himself from the family home, which Dr King said she understood to be true.

Rise and fall of Justin Fairfax JUSTIN Fairfax crashed from lieutenant governor of Virginia to political pariah just years before he shot dead his wife and turned the gun on himself. Here’s a look at the tragic downfall of Fairfax from Ivy League graduate to accused rapist. Lawyer background Fairfax graduated from Duke University in 2000 with a degree in public policy and earned a JD degree from Columbia Law School in 2004

He served as a law clerk for a judge in Virginia until 2010, when he joined the US Attorneys Office for the Eastern District of Virginia as a prosecutor

He ran for state attorney general in 2013 but lost to Mark Herring Political success Fairfax had a brief stint on a reelection campaign and started working for a private law firm

In 2017, he ran for lieutenant governor of Virginia and significantly outraised his two main opponents

After winning the election he started in January 2018, serving part time while also working as a lawyer, which is traditional for the position Horrific allegations In February 2019, Vanessa Tyson, an associate professor at Scripps College in California, said Fairfax allegedly assaulted her in a hotel at the 2004 Democratic National Convention

The two were consensually kissing when Fairfax grabbed the back of her head and starting forcing her to give him oral sex, she alleged

Just days after this surfaced, another woman, Meredith Watson, claimed he raped her when they were undergraduate students at Duke University in 2000

Fairfax defended his innocence in the face of the allegations and hired a team of lawyers to represent him

He wasn’t ever hit with charges, but the accusations led some local politicians to call for his resignation Doomed campaign Fairfax ultimately served the rest of his term and made a bid for governor while he was in office

However, he only clinched a meager 3.54% of votes in the Democratic primary

Fairfax’s last day as lieutenant governor was January 15, 2022

He returned to work as a private attorney after the political blow Murder suicide death On April 15, Fairfax shot and killed his wife in the basement of their home before turning the gun on himself

The two were embroiled in a nasty divorce, with wife Cerina reportedly fighting for primary custody of their teen kids

They were set to return to court for another hearing when the shooting unfolded

He allegedly spiraled into alcoholism after two women accused him of sexual assault in 2019, ending his political career a year after he was elected as lieutenant governor, despite him vowing he was innocent, the filings state.

In 2022, divorce docs allege that he bought a handgun with the children’s horseback riding lesson money.

“[That was] definitely not the Justin I knew,” Dr King said of his recent personal struggles.



“But I have seen Justin through some really tough times…I knew he was going through some things but I thought he would bounce back like he always did.

“You just never know what straw will break the camel’s back and I think it was overload and the marital issues that were the final straw and no one knows another person’s breaking point.

“[It] absolutely never occurred to me that this could happen. Never – it’s not the Justin I knew.”

Cerina, who was a dentist, was granted full custody of their teen children in March and Fairfax was told to leave the house by the end of April, court documents state.



The couple’s next court date was scheduled for April 21, which police believe was a large trigger in the timing of the killing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In a message to Fairfax’s children, a heartbroken Dr King told them, “there’s a community out there who loves you, who will support you, will be here for you whatever you need.

“All you have to do is reach out and you’ll get through it.”

News.title: Trump reveals new White House bunker with bomb shelters, ‘drone-proof ceilings’ and state-of-the art hospital
News.content:
DONALD Trump has revealed details of his new White House nuke-proof mega bunker and ballroom project which is complete with a “state of the art hospital”.

It comes as he slams the “out of control” judge who has forced him to pause above-ground work on the $400million project.





The US President has been ordered to stop work on the above-ground part of his bunker and ballroom plan for the White House.

Judge Richard Leon said Trump had tried to side-step a previous court order by claiming that the ballroom was vital for national security.

Leon said: “National security is not a blank cheque to proceed with otherwise unlawful activity.”

The White House was sued by the National Trust for Historic Preservation over its dramatic plans to replace the East Wing with a new 1,350-person capacity ballroom.

He hit back that the ballroom was “needed now” and that the underground bunker would be “useless” without the above-ground part of the project.

He said the bunker is “wedded to” the above-ground part, and that the project is “all tied together as one big, expensive, and very complex unit, which is vital for national security and military operations of the United States of America”.

The US President boasted that the upper part of the project will include a “state of the art hospital and medical facilities” and “top secret military installations”. They will be protected, he said, by “missile resistant steel”, “drone proof ceilings and roofs” and “bullet, ballistic, and blast proof glass”. Trump has already razed the White House’s East Wing to make way for the bunker and ballroom project. He branded Richard Leon an “out of control Trump Hating, Washington, D.C. District Court Judge”, claiming his decision to block construction “severely jeopardizes the lives and welfare of the people who work, and will be working, at the White House”.

Trump raged that the Judge “is attempting to prevent future Presidents and World Leaders from having a safe and secure large scale Meeting Place”.



He has insisted a ballroom of this scale has been sought for 150 years and that the existing 200-person capacity room is too small.

The plan for Trump’s nuke-proof mega bunker was revealed at the end of March, after the Secret Service warned delays or halts in the construction of the ballroom would pose “national security concern”. The East Wing of the official presidential residence has featured an underground vault since the 1940s. 6 6 6 The original nuclear vault – formally known as the Presidential Emergency Operations Centre – was built after Pearl Harbour. But the East Wing was razed last year to make way for the controversial $400million ballroom project which is being funded privately by Trump and other donors.

The ballroom will be the biggest structural change to the Executive Mansion since the addition of the Truman Balcony overlooking the South Lawn in 1948, even dwarfing the building itself.

Shalom Baranes, the architect who took over the project last year, told a meeting of the National Capital Planning Commission in Washington in January that the ballroom will be approximately 22,000 square feet.

News.title: Staffy owner looks back at puppy video and makes realisation years later
News.content:
Staffy owner looks back at puppy video and makes realisation years later

A Staffordshire bull terrier has captured hearts thanks to his little sleeping quirk - and his owner just can't get enough and believes it makes him the perfect pet

View Image She loves her staffy will all of her heart (stock) (Image: GETTY (STOCK) )

An adorable dog has melted hearts after a wholesome video showed him doing the exact same thing his entire life - and it says everything about how he feels.

‌



The clip, shared by @ayastaffy, starts with the Staffordshire bull terrier fully grown, lying flat on his back in the middle of the kitchen, legs in the air, completely unbothered. The caption reads: "Dad have I always been laying like this?" What follows is basically proof this dog has been living his best, most relaxed life since day one. The video jumps back through time, showing him as a tiny puppy doing the exact same thing - belly up, every time. He’s sprawled out with his littermates, rolled onto his back during tummy rubs, flopped across the grass, stretched out on the sofa, even lying in his owner’s arms - always in that same position, completely relaxed and trusting.

‌



Clip after clip, nothing changes - same pose, same energy, just smaller.

‌



One moment shows him with a paw lazily covering his face, another has him stretched out in the sun, and in every single shot he looks like he doesn’t have a single worry in the world.

But as being belly-up is one of the most vulnerable positions for dogs - it means they feel completely safe, comfortable and protected in their environment.

People in the comments picked up on it straight away, with one user saying: "That means he feels safe and loved."

‌



Another added: "No freakin' way. That’s ridiculous and adorable." A third wrote: "What a perfect little angel."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Someone else summed it up perfectly: "Tummies from day one."

‌



Speaking about sleeping positions, Dr Patrik Holmboe, head veterinarian at Cooper Pet Care, explained what certain styles can reveal about your pet.

In a statement shared by PetMD, he said the belly-up position - often jokingly called 'the dying cockroach' - is a common favourite among breeds like Greyhound.

"You’ll find dogs in the belly-up pose sleeping on their backs with their bellies fully exposed and legs in the air," he explained. "These dogs are playful and loving - or they’re still puppies."

‌



While it might look a little odd, he reassured owners there’s nothing to worry about.

"Dogs typically don’t choose to sleep in uncomfortable positions," he added.

However, he noted that as dogs get older, they may naturally switch to a different sleeping style.

Article continues below

"Belly-up sleeping can put pressure on the spine, so older dogs may move to positions like sleeping on their side instead."

News.title: Tesco fan spots beloved facility back in stores 'everyone's been waiting for'
News.content:
Tesco fan spots beloved facility back in stores 'everyone's been waiting for'

Fans have shared excitement after a shopper uploaded footage of what looked like its return

View 2 Images Some shoppers say they've seen the facility back in their store, despite official confirmation from Tesco (stock image) (Image: Getty )

A beloved facility that was once available to shoppers in many Tesco supermarkets has reportedly been seen in stores once again by fans. Shoppers have shared excitement after a woman uploaded footage of the facility that was gradually removed, or closed, during the 2020 covid-19 pandemic.

‌



Taking to Instagram, a content creator called Ellena, who goes by the username @Ellena.girliemum, claimed that the Tesco supermarket she was in at the time of filming had brought back changing rooms in its F&F clothing section. She didn't say which exact store she was in, or if it applies to all branches, but the video sparked widespread excitement.

‌



Speaking to the camera, she said: "I've got a big update in Tesco F&F, let me show you what everyone has been waiting for, it is amazing." She then turns the camera around to show what looks like an F&F changing room.

‌



She claimed: "Tesco now has fitting rooms, I can't believe it. Let's just actually see that this is real." She then zooms in on a sign showing the fitting room opening hours.

She added: "They now have fitting rooms in Tesco. So, you can try all your clothes on like we used to and not buy 100,000 jeans and then go home, bring them back, get a refund, go back again with a different size. Just to confirm, Tesco now has fitting rooms."

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



In the comment section of Ellena's video, a user called Charla replied: "I saw this the other day! So handy that it’s back." Another called Fiona said: "Thank goodness!!" Another said: "At flipping last!" Amy put: "This is good news! My daughter would cringe when I was trying jeans on over my leggings in the aisles."

Elsewhere, on Facebook, a member named Nadine, who is part of a group called Bargain Lover, uploaded a picture of the same changing rooms in Ellena's video, and wrote in the caption: "CHANGING ROOMS are coming back at F&F in Tesco!" The post has since gone viral with over 1,200 likes and hundreds of comments. Many people have said they "really hope this is true".

As of April 17, Tesco has not issued an official statement on the seemingly reopening of fitting rooms in selected larger supermarkets. Tesco has been approached for comment.

‌



View 2 Images People have shared their excitement online in response to the video (stock image)

Tesco began shutting down or removing F&F changing rooms during the covid-19 pandemic. While a few stores reopened them for a short time, many remained closed for good, largely due to low usage, safety concerns during the pandemic, staffing issues, and theft concerns.

Shoppers have been asking for the changing rooms to return ever since. Many rely on Tesco's return policy to try on clothes. As of early 2026, people on social media are still calling for their reinstatement.

Article continues below

There are mixed reports about some places reopening their changing rooms, but it’s not confirmed whether they are widely available. For the most accurate information about a specific store, use the Tesco Store Locator to check in-store features.

News.title: 'Hallways stay tidy' with Home Bargains £25 storage similar to IKEA version
News.content:
'Hallways stay tidy' with Home Bargains £25 storage similar to IKEA version

The furniture piece could help keep shoes neat and tidy

View 3 Images The unit is available in stores and online (Image: Nathan Stirk/Getty Images)

Home Bargains is selling a storage solution that is "perfect for small spaces" and gets rid of a common clutter issue in homes. It looks very similar to a popular IKEA item at a reduced price.

‌



The simple Utility Two-Tier Shoe Cabinet costs £24.99, and is available to order online or find in one of Home Bargains' 600 stores across the UK. It claims to help eliminate the problem of footwear piling up by the front door in busy homes.

‌



Describing the cabinet online, Home Bargains bosses said: "Keep your hallway neat, tidy, and totally clutter-free with this sleek Two-Tier Shoe Cabinet. Designed with a slim profile that fits perfectly in small spaces, it offers a stylish way to store footwear while keeping everything hidden and organised.

‌



"With room to hold up to eight pairs of shoes, it’s ideal for busy households, sneaker lovers, or anyone who’s tired of tripping over stray footwear. The smooth pull-down compartments make it easy to grab what you need on the go, while the top surface is perfect for plants, candles, or décor that adds personality to your entryway."

The unit is designed to deliver "maximum storage with minimal footprint", measuring 80cm tall, 60cm wide, and 24cm deep. Home Bargains added that hallways should feel "fresher, cleaner, and more put-together" with one of these cabinets.

View 3 Images The Utility Two-Tier Shoe Cabinet (Image: Home Bargains)

‌



The item is very similar to a popular IKEA item that often sells out. The BISSA Shoe Cabinet (£30) comes with two compartments and a smooth white finish.

Shoppers do have the option to go bigger at IKEA, unlike Home Bargains, with a three-tier version (£45). The two-level IKEA version also claims to hold eight pairs of shoes, but it shows that families might be able to squeeze three sets of smaller children's shoes onto a row instead of two pairs.

One other difference is that IKEA's unit is slightly taller and deeper than the Home Bargains option, meaning people working with a limited space might want to consider the smaller size. The Swedish version measures 93cm tall, 49cm wide and 28cm deep.

‌



View 3 Images The similar IKEA BISSA unit (Image: IKEA)

In other Home Bargains news, a £20 coffee table could be a budget-friendly yet 'modern' buy for anyone hoping to 'upgrade their home' this season - and it looks identical to a £50 version available elsewhere. The discount store is known for its range of affordable homeware and furniture.

Describing the store's Home Oak Effect Coffee Table, a spokesperson said: "The Home Oak Effect Coffee Table is a simple and stylish addition to any living space. It’s got a handy lower shelf for extra storage, perfect for books, magazines, or everyday essentials."

Article continues below

The £20 table has similar features to B&Q's HOMCOM Coffee Table with Storage Shelf, which costs £49.99. The online-only item has a minimalistic look and has been designed to fit into any setting, including living rooms, bedrooms, offices and boardrooms.

News.title: Halifax joins HSBC, Santander and TSB with change for customers 'from Friday'
News.content:
Halifax joins HSBC, Santander and TSB with change for customers 'from Friday'

It's had a cautious welcome

View 3 Images Halifax's cuts kick in on Friday (Image: Robert Brook via Getty Images)

Halifax has joined Santander and HSBC in making 'positive' moves this week with a change that begins on Friday. It is slashing its home-mover and first-time buyer fixed rate mortgages by up to 0.35% on Friday, in a move that "feels like the start of a broader repricing" in the market, according to brokers. This follows similar rate reductions from lenders including HSBC, Santander and TSB earlier this week.

‌



Craig Fish, director at London-based Lodestone Mortgages, said: "Halifax joining HSBC and Santander in cutting rates is genuinely positive news and, yes, this does feel like the start of a broader repricing as lenders compete for business in a quieter market. But let's keep things in perspective. Rates are still over 1% higher than before the Middle East conflict began, so while the direction of travel is welcome, we are a long way from where we were.

‌



"Lenders are cutting because swap rates have ticked down slightly, giving them a little room to move. But swaps remain elevated, and with the US still using threatening language tensions could escalate quickly, and rates with them.

‌



"My advice to borrowers? Don't wait for rates to fall back to where you think they should be. That may not happen anytime soon.

"If you're a first-time buyer or homemover, this window of competition between lenders is your opportunity. Speak to a broker, understand your options and act while the market is working in your favour."

View 3 Images HSBC has made changes (Image: whitemay via Getty Images)

‌



Riz Malik, Independent Financial Adviser at Southend-on-Sea-based R3 Wealth, cautiously welcomed the reductions but reminded borrowers that we live in the age of Trump.

He said: "Conditions have improved and Halifax is one of a number of lenders who have pared back on some of their recent hikes. If Trump doesn't start any more wars, we should be able to take a breather. That's a big ask."

Elliott Culley, director at Hayling Island-based Switch Mortgage Finance, said: "Halifax are reducing their rates in line with other mortgage lenders. With tensions in the Middle East still elevated, it raises questions as to why lenders are now willing to reduce rates.

‌



"In reality the swap rates have been fairly consistent over the last two weeks and mortgage lenders priced in much higher swap rates. As this has not materialised, some lenders are now reducing rates to make their products more competitive to borrowers."

View 3 Images Santander has also made cuts (Image: Ceri Breeze via Getty Images)

Emma Jones, managing director at Runcorn-based Whenthebanksaysno.co.uk, cautioned that it is premature to declare this a definitive turning point.

Article continues below

She continued: "It's encouraging to see a handful of big lenders reprice down over the past day or two, but let's remember that the situation in the Middle East remains highly volatile. These cuts could be reversed just as quickly."

Katy Eatenton, mortgage and protection specialist at St Albans-based Lifetime Wealth Management, concurred that Halifax's announcement represents a move in the right direction, but stressed that what truly matters is whether the reductions are both widespread and sustained across the market.

She said: "Rates are still far higher than they were at the end of February, but they are at least now moving in the right direction. The big question now is whether this is a premature move or the beginning of a more sustainable downward repricing."

News.title: NHS worker bravely speaks out after racist couple's vile five-word slur in park
News.content:
NHS worker bravely speaks out after racist couple's vile five-word slur in park

Although she is a British citizen, Apple Moorhouse was racially abused in Manor Heath Park in Halifax, West Yorkshire, an incident which left her "looking over" her shoulder

View 3 Images Apple Moorhouse hit back after her racism ordeal (Image: Newsquest / SWNS)

An NHS worker has spoken of her distress after a racist couple subjected her to vile abuse in a park.

‌



Apple Moorhouse hit back at Fyona Bairstow, 72, and Michael Bairstow, 77, who told the woman to "go back to your dinghy". Apple, who is a British citizen having lived here since 2009, said yesterday the foul-mouthed tirade has left her "scared" and unsettled.

‌



The Bairstows turned on Apple after she asked them to keep her dog on a led in Manor Heath Park in Halifax, West Yorkshire. Sickening video footage which captured incident later went viral, showing the couple — who had been married for three decades — hurling a barrage of abuse at the healthcare worker.

‌



She said yesterday: "It's a big thing, racism, and it needs to be dealt with. I've been here since 2009 and never had anything like this before, for 10 years, it was fine but now it's got worse.

"I used to work in healthcare and I wanted to go back but I felt scared … this happened and I just didn't go back. Caring was my passion but then this happened and it was hard to go back."

Residents at city suburb hit back as Robert Jenrick compares area to a 'slum' READ MORE :

OPINION Ros Wynne Jones 'Some 500,000 Brits choose hope as they take to London streets against far right'

‌



View 3 Images Fyona Bairstow and Michael Bairstow are pictured arriving at court (Image: Newsquest / SWNS)

The Bairstows, who recorded the clip, were both given eight-week jail sentences yesterday at Bradford and Keighley Magistrates' Court. They had admitted racially/religiously aggravated common assault against Apple at a previous hearing.

The charge relates to the incident at Manor Heath Park on August 28, 2025 when Apple ad been in the park with her father and six-year-old daughter. Mr Bairstow also admitted a charge of assault by beating, which was in relation to another woman who tried to intervene.

‌



Sentencing the pair, a magistrate said: "My personally first instinct is it's deeply sickening and the point is usually with age and ageing usually comes wisdom and kindness.

"That kind of attitude and those words and the things you've said to Apple Moorhouse are not something that come out in a second, they're something that are deep-rooted.

"Somebody that can be so vile and aggressive to somebody as this young woman here I can only think you are extremely ashamed both of you."

‌



View 3 Images Apple, a mum from Halifax, spoke following the sentencing (Image: Newsquest / SWNS)

The couple were heard saying they were "ashamed" of their behaviour. During the hearing earlier this year Richard Davies, for the prosecution, outlined the circumstances of the case, describing it as a "nasty incident". It heard how Apple, who is a British citizen, had moved to the UK from the Philippines in 2009.

The court heard the Bairstows were out with their dog, which was "running free" and "wasn't on a lead". Mr Davies said the dog went up to Apple's child and began barking, scaring her, so she intervened.

Article continues below

The Bairstows approached and Ms Moorhouse, who had been in the play area but was heading back due to it raining heavily, said to Mr Bairstow, "your dog should be on a lead because it's been running up to everyone", the court heard. Mr Davies said the reaction was "very hostile" with Mr Bairstow telling her to "go back to your dinghy" and making swimming gestures.

News.title: 'I'm going blind at 36 and can't see my daughter'
News.content:
'I'm going blind at 36 and can't see my daughter'

Kaylie is having to raise money for private surgery

View 5 Images Kaylie with her daughter Boe (Kennedy News & Media)

A mum who assumed she had conjunctivitis as 'only elderly people got cataracts' has been told she is going blind at 36. Kaylie Kelliher first noticed she was struggling with her eyesight in August last year after waking up one morning and discovering everything around her looked 'hazy'.

‌



Initially being told it was conjunctivitis at a pharmacy, the mum-of-one was prescribed eye drops but claims her eyesight kept declining. Kaylie says that lights were 'blinding' her and that during a family camping trip at the end of August she noticed she was struggling to see.

‌



In September, Kaylie visited her optician and was diagnosed with rapid onset cataracts, a condition that usually affects those aged 60 or over. The mum-of-one, who can't see her face in the mirror or watch TV, is now fundraising to have surgery privately in a bid to restore her sight.

‌



View 5 Images Kaylie with her daughter Boe (Kennedy News & Media)

Kaylie who lives in Greenwich, London said: "I was absolutely dumbfounded when he [the optician] said to me I had rapid onset cataracts. I said to him 'I'm too young for that' and he was like 'yes you are, you're really young and it shouldn't be happening at your age'.

"I have really elderly neighbours and I've heard cataracts mentioned from them. I'm not living a life at the minute, I'm housebound. I can't do anything, even just silly girl things. [Like] being able to paint your toenails because you can't see them, or pluck your eyebrows because I can't even see my own face in the mirror.

‌



"I can't even see the telly, I can't see anything, it's hard because it happened so quickly. Facing the possibility of being blind makes me sad."

Kaylie, who is mum to seven-year-old Boe Bushnell, said: "Last summer I noticed that lights weren't even lights anymore, they were becoming like halos. As I was driving at night I noticed the lights were blinding and everyone was saying 'oh all the cars have got all those new LED lights, it's them', but this was just something different.

View 5 Images Kaylie needs surgery to save her sight (Kennedy News & Media)

‌



"I remember rubbing my eyes in the morning and everything seemed so hazy and milky. I went to the pharmacist and they thought I could have conjunctivitis so I was putting eyedrops in and it just kept getting worse. We went camping in August and these were the two weeks when I noticed I was really struggling to see.

"Never in a million years would I have thought it would be cataracts."

Kaylie's eyesight has deteriorated to -12 in her right eye and -11 in her left and without surgery she faces the possibility of going fully blind. A minus number indicates short-sightedness, and the higher the number, the stronger prescription required, with Specsavers classing six as a large number.

‌



View 5 Images Kaylie with her husband Joe (Kennedy News & Media)

Now struggling to see her daughter, Kaylie's sister has set up a GoFundMe page as private treatment is estimated to cost £15,000. Kaylie said: "I struggle to see her [Boe] now. She knows, she rubs my eyes. I feel for her, [when] she breaks up for school holidays I can't take her out, I can't get on a bus. I can't do anything.

"I can't see anything and it's obviously too dangerous to take her out on my own anymore. There is no way we could ever even contemplate having that sort of money for private surgery. It's just something we haven't got."

‌



View 5 Images Kaylie with her husband Joe (Kennedy News & Media)

You can donate to Kaylie's GoFundMe here https://www.gofundme.com/f/help-kay-get-urgent-sightsaving-cataract-surgery

Cataracts are where the lens in your eye becomes cloudy, causing blurred vision and loss of sight. It usually affects older adults and can be treated with surgery.You may be more likely to get cataracts if you're aged 60 or you've had an eye injury or eye surgery in the past.

Article continues below

Cataracts affect your sight and without treatment will eventually cause sight loss.

News.title: 'I thought I had dementia when I started forgetting my sons' names'
News.content:
'I thought I had dementia when I started forgetting my sons' names'

Meera said she felt like she was becoming a 'moron' until finally being diagnosed seven years later

View 3 Images Meera Mehat thought she had early onset dementia (Image: SWNS)

A mum thought she had early onset dementia when she forgot her sons' names. Meera Mehat, 59, was 49 when she began having difficulty recalling words during presentations at work.

‌



The mum-of-three, from Maidenhead, Berkshire, initially put it down to work stress, until she forgot all three of her sons' names when introducing them. She feared she had early-onset dementia and went to doctors for brain scans, but when they came back clear, she was reassured it was just a sign of aging.

‌



Meera found the process so "frightening" that she quit her job and stopped going out - after she struggled to hold conversations with friends. She even forgot her son's birthday until a family member called her on the day - realising she never bought presents, a cake, or planned a party.

‌



It was only when someone suggested she went to a private doctor seven years on, when it was put down to "menopausal issues". After being given a hormone-friendly diet and hormone supplements, along with an exercise and meditation schedule, Meera - who now works as a menopause educator- noticed her memory improving.

Getting married could save your life, frozen dead man brought back, fruit and veg win Alzheimer's fight, and scientists find 'natural Ozempic' that comes without the annoying side effects - all this and more in our latest science newsletter

She said despite endless scans, tests, and doctors' appointments, it took seven years for someone to mention menopause to her - all the while leaving her feeling she was "going mad".

‌



View 3 Images Meera is mum to Jas, Kash, and Alekh (Image: SWNS)

Meera, mum to twins Jas and Kash, 27, and Alekh, 25, said: "First, I struggled to remember stats when I was training people at work - and I had written the damn training programme.

"Over time, when I met friends and I'd start telling a story, I'd forget the words, and by the time I'd found them, I'd forgotten when I was talking about. People said it was normal aging but I thought I had early-onset dementia.

‌



"In the end I stopped working and stopped going out - it became too much effort to even think. I became a moron. But brain scans showed nothing wrong - and that terrified me even more. Nobody knew what was happening to me.

"After seeing the private doctor, I followed the advice and in three months I felt like a complete different person. I want to empower other women now - I wonder how many other women are being fobbed off that it's just a sign of normal aging."

Meera first noticed issues aged 49, in 2015, when she was presenting a training program at work, and forgot all her data. She had recently moved into a new role and put it down to the stress, until it began happening outside of work too.

‌



She said: "I couldn't make sentences properly and forgot what I was saying." She burst into tears on her 50th birthday because she was too afraid of what was happening to celebrate.

Doctors simply told her it "will resolve itself". Meera said: "I forgot my son Alekh's birthday completely - I hadn't bought gifts, hadn't planned anything, it hadn't even occurred to me.

"I remember calling one of my sons my dog's name once. And another time, I went to introduce my sons to someone and forgot all their names.

‌



"You get good at not talking and covering it up. You ask them questions, make them fill the gap. You do it so people don't know you're not functioning."

View 3 Images Meera now works as a menopause educator (Image: SWNS)

Even at home, she forgot recipes she had been making for her family for years. She would sit at home watching TV, to the concern of supportive husband Narb, 63, and wouldn't sleep at night.

‌



In 2021, she got an MRI scan but it came back completely normal. Meera said: "That terrified me even more. I was thinking, am I getting dementia? Am I hallucinating? Am I going mad?"

But after visiting a private doctor in 2022, he suggested it might be the menopause. She was given a food plan without any sugar or gluten and minimal dairy, and her protein intake was upped.

She was given "a barrage of supplements and treatments" including oestrogen and magnesium. She was also given an exercise plan including walking, strength training and stretching, and mandatory relaxation activities including meditation.

‌



She was told to try her new hormone-friendly and reduced-inflammatory diet for three to six months, and to her surprise and delight, by the third month, she could already notice differences. She began taking hormone replacement therapy too, and things continued to improve.

Meera said: "I'm pretty much back to normal now - and I'm not scared to go out and meet people any more." She said: "Education is getting better, but it's still vague around menopause. But there are studies to show brain fog is real and it's miserable."

Meera has now developed an app to help other women, called Menopause Meditation - which won an award for the 'Best Menopause Cognitive Health Solution' at this year's Menopause In Practice awards.

Article continues below

According to the Faculty of Occupational Medicine within the NHS, 75-80% of menopausal women are still in work. She said: "It's becoming more of an issue now because we're an aging population, women are having children later, and they're also stepping up getting more senior roles at work."

According to the Faculty of Occupational Medicine within the NHS, 75-80% of menopausal women are still in work. Meera added: "Women need support but they don't know what there is. HRT is good but there is more you can do.

"I'd like to empower others - half the issue is the stress of it and wondering if you're going mad."

News.title: Judge stops sentencing of serial burglar after seeing he has 26 birthdays
News.content:
Judge stops sentencing of serial burglar after seeing he has 26 birthdays

Anthony Paul Maughan pleaded guilty to a string of thefts across Wales, but his sentencing was held up by judge after it was found he had dozens of listed birthdays

View 2 Images Anthony Paul Maughan was not sentenced due to his dozens of birthdays (Image: Media Wales)

A judge was forced to halt sentencing a defendant in court after he was confronted with his 26 different birthdays - and ordered him into the witness box instead.

‌



Anthony Paul Maughan, of no fixed abode, was due to be sentenced this week after pleading guilty to 10 counts of non-dwelling burglary and one count of theft from a vehicle, and had appeared in the dock as he awaited Judge Huw Rees' ruling. He had embarked on a burglary spree across Wales, hitting cafes, restaurants and shops in Swansea, Neath, Bridgend and Cardiff.

‌



But the "persistent offender" wasn't sentenced when originally planned after the judge said he wasn't prepared to hand down a decision without knowing which one of Maughan's 26 dates of birth was correct.

‌



Should balaclavas be banned in the UK? Take our poll and have your say READ MORE :

Seven tips to stop thieves stealing your petrol amid Iran war crime wave READ MORE :

View 2 Images Maughan was found to have 26 different birthdays, and ordered to attend court as a witness to straighten out the issue (Image: Getty Images/iStockphoto)

Wales Online reports that Judge Rees adjourned the hearing and ordered Maughan, then appearing via videolink, to be brought to the court in person. He also asked the prosecution to conduct their own enquiries to discover the defendant's true date of birth.

Prosecutors had earlier told the court about Maughan's 18-day burglary spree. Matthew Comer told Swansea Crown Court that the defendant had spent the nearly 20 days in January and February burgling 10 businesses.

‌



His targets included the Giggling Squid restaurant, a Tesco Express shop, Castle Welsh Crafts shop, Total Asia restaurant, and Cote Brasserie - all in Cardiff alone.

The prosecution also said he had raided a Costa Coffee in Bridgend, Kumar Stores in Neath, and an Aldi supermarket, Fresco Cafe, and Green Room restaurant in Swansea.

Barristers added that, over the same period, Maughan committed theft from a vehicle when he entered a lorry cab as the driver made a delivery in Cardiff.

Article continues below

In a number of burglaries, the court heard, he had entered staff only areas while business premises were open, and had also forced entry to businesses via closed rear doors or fire exits while the buildings were closed. Maughan was placed at the scene of each of his 10 thefts via the use of CCTV.

Prosecutors told the court that Maughan put together a significant haul of items from his sprees, including bank cards, jackets from North Face, keys, iPhones, meats and cheeses, bottles of whisky, vodka and champagne, and a brand-new pair of Adidas trainers.

He was also found to have taken various quantities of cash. Judge Rees adjourned sentencing until April 29, with Maughan further remanded into custody until his next court appearance.

News.title: Rain set to ease for the weekend as sunshine returns
News.content:
Our analysis of rainfall data shows that parts of East Anglia and the south-east of England have been very dry.

Across the county of Essex, around a fifth of the rain we'd usually expect by this time in spring has actually fallen.

In the month of March, rainfall was broadly below average in eastern and south-east England, April has started even drier.

According to Met Office data, between 1 - 14 April there has only been 4.5mm of rain compared to the average of around 20mm for the time of the year

In contrast, Western Scotland has had around double of its normal April rainfall so far.

During March things were broadly average across Scotland but a succession of weather systems in April has brought a lot of rainfall.

Looking just at April, an average of 70mm fell across the whole of Scotland compared to the 40mm you'd usually expect at this stage of the month.

While a lot can change in the second half of spring, the mostly dry weather is likely to continue into next week.

Droughts and hosepipe bans featured widely in 2025 after the driest spring in 50 years and the hottest summer on record.

But in late March 2026 - after one of the wettest winters since 1836 - the Environment Agency confirmed that eastern England the last region still in 'recovery' to 'normal' conditions.

News.title: Watch: Reporter told to fake domestic abuse claim to remain in the UK
News.content:
Migrants are falsely claiming to be victims of domestic abuse in order to stay in the country, exploiting rules brought in to expedite the process of securing permanent residence for genuine abuse victims

A BBC investigation has found that legal advisers are encouraging some to make up abuse allegations. One of those advisers, Eli Ciswaka, encouraged a BBC reporter to make false allegations of domestic abuse - saying that he would fabricate the claim for £900, creating a story to tell the Home Office in order to secure the client's status in the UK.

Ciswaka did not respond to a written request for comment, but during a phone call to tell him about our investigation he denied being willing to make up a story that the undercover reporter had been a victim of domestic abuse.

News.title: Bad bromance: Trump slams Mayor Zohran Mamdani and claims he’s ‘destroying’ New York with tax policies
News.content:

President Donald Trump has turned on New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani just months after their surprisingly friendly encounter at the White House, accusing the latter of “destroying” his hometown through tax initiatives.

“Sadly, Mayor Mamdani is DESTROYING New York!” the president wrote on Truth Social late Thursday.

“It has no chance! The United States of America should not contribute to its failure. It will only get WORSE. The TAX, TAX, TAX Policies are SO WRONG. People are fleeing. They must change their ways, AND FAST. History has proven, THIS ‘STUFF’ JUST DOESN’T WORK.”

open image in gallery President Donald Trump and New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani enjoyed a highly cordial first meeting at the White House, making the former’s latest attack all the more surprising ( Donald Trump/Truth Social )

It was not immediately clear what prompted the attack, but there is little evidence to suggest that people are “fleeing” New York in opposition to Mamdani’s policies.

The Independent has reached out to the White House and City Hall for comment.

The attack was all the more surprising given that the two men enjoyed a cordial first meeting when Mamdani visited the Oval Office in November shortly after beating Andrew Cuomo in the Big Apple’s mayoral race.

The candidate shrugged off doubts about his experience by running a superbly well-organized grassroots campaign in which he made no secret of his intention to place higher taxes on the wealthy to level the playing field and make the city more affordable for the less fortunate.

Despite being poles apart politically and Trump having branded Mamdani a “100% Communist Lunatic” during his campaign and threatened to cut federal funding if he won, the duo got along famously in person.

“I think you're going to have, hopefully, a really great mayor – the better he does, the happier I am,” the president said at the time.

“I will say there’s no difference in party. There’s no difference in anything, and we’re going to be helping him to make everybody’s dream come true, having a strong and very safe New York.”

open image in gallery Mamdani and Trump traded insults while the former was campaigning to lead the Big Apple but had largely kept up a more diplomatic tone since his victory, until now ( Donald Trump/Truth Social )

For his part, Mamdani described their sitdown as “productive” and “focused on a place of shared admiration and love” between him and Trump – New York City – and “the need to deliver affordability to New Yorkers, the eight and a half million people who call our city their home, who are struggling to afford life in the most expensive city in the United States of America.

“We spoke about rent, we spoke about groceries, we spoke about utilities. We spoke about the different ways in which people are being pushed out. And I appreciated the time with the President. I appreciated the conversation. I look forward to working together to deliver that affordability for New Yorkers.”

The mayor even got away with having previously labeled Trump a “fascist,” which, when raised by a reporter, led the president to reassure him: “That’s OK – you can just say ‘yes.’”

They met again two days after Trump had pivoted back to attacking him at the State of the Union in late February, at which he disparaged Mamdani as “the new communist mayor of New York City” for opposing a new Republican-led voter ID bill, summing him up as “bad policy, but a nice guy.”

The mayor also described their second meeting as “productive,” preferring to keep the tone diplomatic, adding in a post on X (Twitter) that he was “looking forward to building more housing in New York City” as a result of their conversation.

Clarkson’s Farm star Harriet Cowan has reflected on giving the straight-shooting Jeremy Clarkson a taste of his own medicine in the hit Amazon series.

Cowan, 25, became the breakout star of the hit Prime Video series after she temporarily replaced farm manager Kaleb Cooper in last year’s fourth season.

The former full-time nurse won over audiences with her witty asides and impressive farming knowledge. She was also praised for standing her ground with Clarkson, with the TV host himself calling her “brilliant”.

Speaking about her no-nonsense attitude on screen in The Times, Cowan said: “If a bloke thinks he knows better than me and starts talking s***, I’ll tell him so.”

She continued: “When I was on Clarkson’s Farm telling Jeremy what I thought, that was the real me. It wasn’t put on for the cameras.”

Cowan did not shy away from telling Clarkson what she thought. It was not long before she was telling him off for his poor management of the hedges and pointing out that the squeaky cow brush needs a dose of WD40 – an aerosol spray that helps with lubrication.

Her straight-talking dealings with the ex-Top Gear presenter earned Cowan a large fanbase, who also took a shine to her sense of humour.

In episode one of the season, Clarkson gives Cowan a tour of the farm. At one point, he identifies a Neolithic fort, which he explains is “4000 years old”, prompting Cowan to quip: “Nearly as old as you.” She even attempts to trim Clarkson’s unruly eyebrows.

open image in gallery Lisa Hogan, Jeremy Clarkson, Kaleb Cooper, Harriet Cowan and Charlie Ireland pose after winning the 'Factual Entertainment' award during the NTA's 2025 at The O2 Arena on September 10, 2025 in London, England. (Photo by Joe Maher/Getty Images for the NTA's) ( Getty )

Cowan, whose dad is a farmer, graduated from the University of Derby, where she studied nursing. She was offered a spot on Clarkson’s Farm while she was working in community nursing.

She recently quit medicine to pursue farming full-time. “There was a period where I thought I could do both but when I was doing home visits, some of the patients started recognising me,” she said. “I’m trying to take their blood pressure and they want to know about me sitting behind Alison Hammond at the National Television Awards.”

Cowan was named her town’s Young Farmers spokesperson and continues to use social media to highlight the realities of working on a farm.

Her social media presence has been credited with sparking an interest in agriculture as a Gen Z career choice. On the subject of her influence, Cowan said: “People have said that me being on telly has got more young people, especially girls, interested in farming, but British farmers aren’t getting support, so there aren’t many jobs.

“Brexit should have made things better for farmers but we’re still importing too much as it’s cheaper. We could be self-sufficient in far more foods but we have to get away from the idea of everything costing next to nothing.”

open image in gallery Kaleb Cooper and Harriet Cowan on 'Clarkson's Farm' ( Prime Video )

Cowan has previously been vocal during the farmers’ protests in response to Labour’s changes to inheritance tax, which saw thousands of farmers gather in Westminster last year.

While she hopes to do more television in the future, she is now focused on buying her own farm with her partner, James Booth. “At the moment I work on my family’s farm, plus do any freelance work I can pick up,” she said.

The next season of Clarkson’s Farm is reportedly currently in production and is scheduled for release on Prime Video in May 2026.

open image in gallery ( TikTok/@harrietcowan3 )

The series will feature its most heartbreaking scenes yet, with episodes expected to focus on the outbreak of bovine tuberculosis, which struck the Cotswolds farm in October 2025.

Bovine TB (bTB) is a chronic respiratory disease caused by a bacterium called Mycobacterium bovis. The disease can be catastrophic for farmers and forces the culling of infected cattle. Due to a bTB incident in England between October 2021 and September 2022, 22,934 cows were killed.

Following the success of Cowan’s stint on the fourth season, fans have requested that she return for season five. Whether she will is yet to be confirmed.

Cash-Out and In-Play exclusions

News.content:

Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. After a period dominated by understated, plain pink manicures, a new wave of nail art is sweeping through salons, bringing with it a desire for movement and fluidity.

The latest technique capturing attention is ‘blooming gel’, a Japanese-born innovation promising unique, diffused designs where no two creations ever look quite the same.

At its core, blooming gel is a clear, highly fluid gel with a lower viscosity than standard nail varnish. This unique consistency allows it to disperse colour in ways traditional formulas cannot, creating distinctive patterns.

Rhiannon Thayre, a nail art specialist from Paint Nails London, explains: "Blooming gel creates soft, diffused designs like marble, aura or reptile effects." She adds, "It gently spreads outwards on its own, creating a blurred, almost misty finish without needing too much precision."

Unlike conventional gel applications, the blooming gel is not immediately cured. Instead, pigment is introduced while the gel is still wet, enabling it to expand organically across the nail. Lead nail technician Jordan Smith elaborates: "It’s essentially a clear gel with a very thin consistency. You apply it over a cured base, then drop pigment into it and watch it bloom. Because it’s so fluid, the colour blends seamlessly […] you can actually see the design forming before you lock it in."

The burgeoning popularity of blooming gel can be attributed to several factors. "It’s trending because it creates a softer, more toned-down finish compared to bold or highly defined designs. Clients are leaning towards something more effortless," Thayre notes. Beyond its aesthetic, the technique offers undeniable visual appeal. The mesmerising process of pigment feathering into soft halos or expanding into marble-like veins has become a staple of hypnotic manicure videos online.

"It’s very satisfying to watch," Smith says, "and it fits with the wider move towards more fluid, organic nail designs. It looks elevated, but it’s actually quite accessible." High-profile figures such as Dua Lipa and Hailey Bieber have further propelled its rise, embracing these diffused manicures. Crucially, blooming gel aligns with a broader shift in beauty, moving away from rigid, minimalist nails towards more expressive and less 'perfect' styles.

For those considering a blooming gel manicure, the options are vast. Emi Nomura, a nail technician at Shoreditch Nails, highlights the creative freedom: "The fun thing about blooming gel is that there are endless options with what you can create, from beautiful watery effects to layered florals."

She adds, "We use it most often to create large flowers and snake prints. You can also use it to make a marbled effect or tortoiseshell print." A key distinction of this technique, as Smith points out, is its departure from traditional nail art's emphasis on precision. "Traditional nail art is about clean lines and precision. With blooming gel, it’s about movement. The product does a lot of the work for you."

While blooming gel manicures are predominantly salon-based, enthusiasts can experiment with the technique at home. Thayre advises on the essential kit: "You’ll need a base colour, blooming gel, pigmented shades, a brush or dotting tool, and a UV or LED lamp."

She stresses the importance of speed: "The key is to work quickly, because the gel will continue to spread until you cure it." Smith recommends a methodical approach: "Work on one nail at a time so you can control how much the design develops."

open image in gallery Snake skin purple blooming gel nails by Hollie at Shoreditch Nails ( Shoreditch Nails )

For those without gel-specific tools, a similar effect can be achieved using conventional nail varnish. Nomura suggests: "We sometimes suggest using a wet top coat to mimic the effect. You can gently glide colour into it and watch it bloom, but you won’t have the same level of control."

To truly make blooming gel designs stand out, playing with contrast is key, a trend currently dominating salons. At Shoreditch Nails, Nomura observes: "pastel blues are huge right now. A light blue base with brighter blue details for a snake print feels very fresh."

For the summer months, vibrant neons like lime and fuchsia, alongside oceanic tones such as teal, white, and deep blue, are gaining traction, particularly when layered over sheer bases to enhance the sense of movement.

open image in gallery Ocean blue blooming gel nails by Hannah at Shoreditch Nails ( Shoreditch Nails )

For a more understated yet impactful look, nail artist Hannah Johnson suggests: "you can achieve the classic tortoiseshell using blooming gel, layered with glass colours, to really add that depth. Animal prints are a neutral in our world!" Whether opting for bold neons or subtle neutrals, the overarching trend points towards strong, expressive patterns.

The blooming gel trend signifies a vibrant return to expressive nail art, offering a versatile and visually captivating alternative to minimalist styles. Its blend of effortless elegance and creative freedom ensures its place as a significant beauty trend.
